title: SCRAP YARD '95

selected_categories.reasoning: The central pleasure loop is spawning objects and deliberately smashing them together so they disappear in explosive audiovisual feedback.
The game emphasizes tactile drag interactions, punchy sound cues, particle bursts, and low-stakes spectacle over challenge.
Objects move with velocity, friction, bounce, and collision checks, but there are no authored puzzle goals; this is a weak partial match based on interaction feel.
It can be soothing in a toy-like sensory sense, but the tone is louder and more chaotic than true ASMR or calm relaxation design.
It is sandbox-like and open-ended, but there is no actual building or construction system, so this only fits the unstructured play shape.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not include an exact 'physics sandbox' or 'destruction toy' label, so the best fit is approximate.
The game is not truly a builder, runner, shooter, tycoon, puzzle campaign, or simulator in the realistic management sense.
Physics puzzle ranks only because movement and collisions matter; the absence of explicit puzzle objectives lowers confidence.
